construction_markdown:
Fix `F=F_2[T]/(T^30+T+1)`, with `theta=T mod (T^30+T+1)`, and enumerate `F` by its 30 polynomial-basis bits. Let `L_65` contain all odd polynomials `P(X)=sum_{1<=j<=65, j odd} a_j X^j` over `F`. For an explicitly based binary subspace `V<=F^2`, define

`C(V)={ (c+Tr(P(x)+a x^67+b x^69))_{x in F} : c in F_2, P in L_65, (a,b) in V }`.

The evaluation map is injective, so `dim C(V)=991+dim_F2(V)`. The proved anchor is `C(0)`, the existing explicit `[2^30,991,>=535822336]_2` degree-65 trace code. A candidate exceeding the proved campaign construction of dimension 1040 would require `dim(V)>=50`. This report proves that such a safe `V` exists if and only if the full choice `V=F^2` is safe. The latter would give the completely explicit dimension-1051 code using every odd exponent through 69, but its required character-sum bound remains unproved.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For algebraic positions 4 and 6: let `C(V)=C_65 + {Tr(a x^67+b x^69):(a,b) in V}`. A Chevalley–Warning argument, plus a checked codimension-10 parity lemma, proves that every `V<=F_(2^30)^2` of binary dimension at least 50 meets every weighted orbit `{(a u^67,b u^69):u!=0}`. Hence a target-safe `V` of dimension at least 50 exists iff the full degree-69 trace code is target-safe. The only outcomes in this architecture are therefore no improvement beyond 1040, or the full explicit `k=1051` code; searching for a special 50-dimensional selector is unnecessary.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For algebraic position 5: if `Q<=RM(2,30)` and `C_65+Q` meets the target, then `dim(C_65+Q)<=1014`. Target-safe quadratic spaces containing all affine phases have polar rank distance at least 18 and hence dimension at most 234 by the Delsarte–Goethals alternating-rank bound. `C_65` already contains an exact 211-dimensional quadratic Gold subcode, leaving at most 23 new quadratic dimensions. Thus quadratic, Gold, Kasami, Kerdock, and Delsarte–Goethals additions cannot beat the existing `k=1040` construction.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For the BCH/character-sum architect: determine whether every odd polynomial `f` of degree at most 69 over `F_(2^30)` satisfies `|sum_x (-1)^Tr(f(x))|<=2^21`. A uniform proof immediately gives an explicit `[2^30,1051,>=535822336]_2` code. One explicit counterexample rules out every dimension-at-least-1041 extension using only the degree-67 and degree-69 coefficient layers. Ordinary Hasse–Weil gives only `68*2^15`, so a saving of `4*2^15` is exactly required.
references: F. Scholten and H. J. Zhu, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0012178

distance_audit: The target is `D=2^29-2^20=535822336`; its equivalent two-sided signed-sum cap is `2^30-2D=2^21=2097152`.
For `C(0)`, every nonzero reduced polynomial has odd degree at most 65. The Artin–Schreier bound gives `|S(P)|<=(65-1)2^15=2^21`, so every nonzero word and its complement have weight at least `D`.
The degree-67 full layer has dimension 1021, but generic Hasse–Weil proves only `d>=2^29-33*2^15=535789568`, missing the target by 32768.

The degree-69 full code has dimension 1051, but generic Hasse–Weil proves only `d>=2^29-34*2^15=535756800`, missing the target by 65536. The unresolved requirement is the sharper uniform cap `64*2^15` instead of `68*2^15`.
For every `V`, target distance is equivalent to `|sum_x (-1)^Tr(P(x)+a x^67+b x^69)|<=2^21` for every nonzero balanced phase, because the external constant supplies the complement of each word.

Pure monomials are not the bottleneck: `S(a x^67)=0` for `a!=0`, while `S(b x^69)` is 65536 for cube `b` and -32768 for either noncube class. These values do not control the required maxima after arbitrary `P in L_65`.
For quadratic phases, the Walsh spectrum and the target cap force every nonzero polar form to have rank at least 18; this is the input to the proved dimension ceilings 234 and 1014.
explicitness_audit: The field is the fixed quotient by `T^30+T+1`; the durable degree-30 Rabin certificate checks Frobenius exponents 6, 10, 15, and 30.
Coordinates are all `2^30` polynomial-basis field elements in lexicographic bit order. No puncturing, padding, sampling, or hidden ordering is used for `C(0)` or the full degree-69 code.
The 991 anchor rows are the all-one row and `Tr(theta^i x^j)` for the 33 odd exponents `j<=65` and `0<=i<30`. The full conditional degree-69 matrix adds the analogous 60 rows for exponents 67 and 69.
The generator algorithm streams every one of the `k*n` bits in deterministic polynomial time; it does not invoke search for a code or a distance witness.

The 5,995,866-case enumeration used in the codimension-10 obstruction is a fully specified finite proof check, independently recomputed from the displayed 30-bit mask. It selects no generator matrix and is smaller than `n`, so it is not an inadmissible exhaustive construction.
No conditional-expectation selector, random sampling, canonical exhaustive code search, or unavailable lookup table is used.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Represent `F` in the polynomial basis `1,theta,...,theta^29`. Enumerate columns by integers `x=0,...,2^30-1`, interpreted as coefficient bitmasks. Output row 0 as all ones. For each odd `j` from 1 through 65 and each `i=0,...,29`, output the row whose `x` entry is `Tr(theta^i x^j)`. This is the complete `991 by 2^30` matrix of the proved anchor. For any explicitly supplied binary basis `(a_t,b_t)` of `V`, append the row `Tr(a_t x^67+b_t x^69)`; for `V=F^2`, use `(theta^i,0)` and `(0,theta^i)` for `0<=i<30`, producing the full conditional `1051 by 2^30` matrix.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(k*n*(log n)^3)` bit operations and `O(log n)` auxiliary bits beyond the streamed output; in particular this is `n^{O(1)}`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: With `m=log_2 n=30`, naive multiplication modulo the fixed degree-30 polynomial costs `O(m^2)` bit operations. Binary powering to exponents at most 69 and the absolute trace, computed by 29 repeated squarings and additions, cost `O(m^3)` per entry under a conservative bound. There are exactly `k*n` entries, so the stated bound follows. Since `k<=1051<=n`, it is at most `O(n^2(log n)^3)` and hence polynomial in `n`; the output itself contains `Theta(k*n)` bits.

proof_markdown:
## 1. Anchor and target cap

For a Boolean phase `f:F->F_2`, write `S(f)=sum_x (-1)^f(x)`. Its truth-table weight is `(q-S(f))/2`. Since the construction contains the external constant 1, it contains both `f` and `f+1`; hence the target is equivalent, apart from the zero and all-one phases, to `|S(f)|<=q-2D=2^21`.

For nonzero `P in L_65`, the smooth model of `y^2+y=P(x)` has genus `(deg(P)-1)/2<=32`. Hasse–Weil therefore gives `|S(P)|<=64*2^15=2^21`. It also prevents a nonzero parameter tuple from evaluating to an affine constant, proving injectivity and `dim C(0)=1+33*30=991`. This reproduces the durable degree-65 trace lemma.

## 2. Weighted scaling

Define

`M(a,b)=max_{P in L_65} |sum_x (-1)^Tr(P(x)+a x^67+b x^69)|`.

For `u!=0`, substitution `x=u y` permutes `F` and maps `L_65` bijectively to itself. Consequently

`M(a,b)=M(a u^67,b u^69)`.

Call `V` safe when `M(a,b)<=2^21` for every `(a,b) in V`, with the already-safe zero-pair interpreted through `C_65`.

## 3. Orbit hitting below codimension 10

If `V<=F^2` has codimension `c`, write it as the common kernel of trace-linear forms `ell_1,...,ell_c`. For a fixed pair `(a,b)`, put

`F_i(u)=ell_i(a u^67,b u^69)`.

The binary expansions `67=2^6+2+1` and `69=2^6+4+1` show that every `F_i`, in 30 binary coordinates for `u`, has algebraic degree at most 3. If `c<=9`, then `sum_i deg(F_i)<=27<30`. Chevalley–Warning makes the number of common zeros even. Since `u=0` is a common zero, another zero has `u!=0`; hence every weighted scaling orbit meets `V`.

## 4. The codimension-10 boundary

For completeness, the equality case is settled by a finite parity certificate. After scalar extension, the Moore coordinates `Y_r=u^(2^r)`, `r in Z/30`, are an invertible linear coordinate system. The cubic parts of the check equations lie in the span of

`Y_r Y_(r+1) Y_(r+6)` and `Y_r Y_(r+2) Y_(r+6)`.

For ten checks, the common-zero count modulo 2 equals

`sum_u product_i(1+F_i(u))`.

All terms of total degree below 30 sum to zero over `F_2^30`. A degree-30 contribution requires ten allowed triples to partition `Z/30`. The assertion is coordinate-independent: the coefficient of a product of all 30 independent linear coordinates changes by the Moore determinant, while any repeated coordinate gives a determinant with repeated rows and contributes zero in characteristic two.

It remains to exclude the exact cover. In `R=F_2[x]/(x^30-1)`, set

`A=1+x+x^6`, `B=1+x^2+x^6`, and `J=1+x+...+x^29`.

Direct cyclic multiplication gives an inverse of `A` with support

`{0,2,3,4,6,7,9,12,15,16,17,21,23,24,25,26,29}`

and gives `D=A^(-1)B=0x11c96ecc`, of support

`{2,3,6,7,9,10,11,13,14,16,19,22,23,24,28}`.

If `a_r,b_r` mark selected triples of the two types, an exact cover implies `Aa+Bb=J` over `F_2`, hence `a=J+Db`. It also implies `wt(a)+wt(b)=10`, so `wt(Db)=20+wt(b)`. Summing covered vertex labels modulo 3 gives `wt(b)=2,5`, or `8`.

The exhaustive verifier is fully specified: for each `k in {2,5,8}` and each lexicographic `k`-subset `I` of `{0,...,29}`, compute `z=XOR_{i in I} rot30(0x11c96ecc,i)` and record `popcount(z)`. The independently recomputed totals and maxima are

| `k` | subsets | maximum `popcount(z)` | required |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 435 | 20 | 22 |
| 5 | 142506 | 23 | 25 |
| 8 | 5852925 | 26 | 28 |

Thus no exact cover exists. The common-zero count is even also at codimension 10, and the zero solution again forces a nonzero solution.

## 5. All-or-nothing degree-69 frontier

Every `V` with `dim(V)>=50` has codimension at most 10 and therefore meets every weighted orbit. If such a `V` is safe, scaling invariance makes every pair in `F^2` safe. Hence `C(F^2)`, the full odd-degree-through-69 trace code, is safe and has dimension 1051. Conversely, if the full code is safe then every subspace is safe. Therefore

`there exists a safe V with dim(V)>=50` if and only if `the full k=1051 code is safe`.

This is a reduction, not a proof that the full code is safe.

## 6. Quadratic phase ceiling

Let `U<=RM(2,30)` contain `RM(1,30)`. For a quadratic phase `Q` with polar form of rank `r`, a standard squaring calculation gives Walsh values either zero or of magnitude `2^(30-r/2)` after affine shifts; some shift attains the nonzero magnitude. The target cap forces `r>=18` for every nonzero polar form.

Polarization maps `U` to an alternating rank-metric code, with kernel exactly `RM(1,30)` of dimension 31. The Delsarte–Goethals bound at `n=30`, field size 2, and rank distance 18 gives image size at most

`2^[30*29/(2*15) * (15-9+1)] = 2^203`.

Thus `dim(U)<=31+203=234`.

Inside `C_65`, the phases

`c+Tr(bx+sum_{i=1}^6 a_i x^(2^i+1))`

form an exact 211-dimensional quadratic subcode. Indeed, if `s<=6` is the largest active index, the radical is the kernel of

`L(x)=sum_{i=1}^s (a_i x^(2^i)+a_i^(2^(30-i)) x^(2^(30-i)))`.

Raising to `2^s` produces a nonzero linearized polynomial of ordinary degree `2^(2s)`, so the radical has dimension at most `2s<=12` and the polar rank is at least 18. This also proves coefficient injectivity; including affine phases gives dimension `1+30+6*30=211`.

Now suppose `C_65+Q` is target-safe for some quadratic subspace `Q`, and put `R=(C_65+Q) intersect RM(2,30)`. Then `dim R<=234` and `dim(R intersect C_65)>=211`. The natural quotient injection

`Q/(Q intersect C_65) -> R/(R intersect C_65)`

shows that at most 23 new dimensions are possible. Therefore `dim(C_65+Q)<=991+23=1014`.

## 7. Landscape conclusion

The generic fixed-conductor Artin–Schreier route, generalized-Niho root-evaluation families, exact-length norm-trace specializations, and arbitrary quadratic augmentations all stop below 1041. The sole surviving trace-polynomial gateway identified here is the universal degree-69 character-sum statement. Current Hasse–Weil gives `68*2^15`; the target requires `64*2^15`.

theorem_statement: Let `F=F_(2^30)`, let `L_65` be the 990-dimensional coefficient space of odd polynomials of degree at most 65, and let `C(V)` augment its trace evaluations by coefficients `(a,b)` from a binary subspace `V<=F^2` on `x^67,x^69`, together with the external constant. Then `dim C(V)=991+dim(V)`. A target-safe `V` with `dim(V)>=50` exists if and only if the full `V=F^2` is target-safe; thus this architecture either gives the full explicit `k=1051` degree-69 code or gives no improvement over the existing `k=1040` campaign construction. Separately, every target-safe quadratic phase space containing all affine phases has dimension at most 234, and every quadratic augmentation of the degree-65 trace code has dimension at most 1014. The full degree-69 distance statement remains unresolved, so this is a proof-tool handoff, not a leaderboard submission.
